newsitem.title: USA: Clinton saves shopping for Sunday before Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Clinton saves shopping for Sunday before Christmas.

text.p: President Bill Clinton spent more than an hour Christmas shopping on Sunday, browsing in an elegant arcade in Washington's historic Union Station.
Clinton browsed quietly among the wood and glass kiosks in the railroad station's East Hall, examining pieces of jewelry and wooden curios among other items.
Wearing a double-breasted blazer adorned with a Santa pin and a red tie, Clinton did his Christmas shopping without his wife Hillary or daughter Chelsea.
Reporters were kept a few dozen yards (metres) from the president, but could see him walking among the East Hall's eight kiosks, making several purchases and paying with a credit card.
Aurea Singh, owner of the Aurea kiosk, which sells Asian, African and South American jewelry and handicrafts, declined to say what Clinton bought, saying it was against her policy.
The East Hall was cordoned off from the station's barrel-vaulted main hall, where several hundred people gathered to watch Clinton shop, at times softly singing Christmas carols.
Union Station, which opened in 1907, was renovated in the 1980s, reopening in 1988 with its two wings transformed into elegant shops and restaurants.
As Clinton left the railroad station at the end of his shopping expedition, two AIDS activists shouted "Shame, Shame, Shame" and "Your AIDS plan's a sham."
